Rethinking Layouts

Search is a core primitive for modern systems, and yet the way most pages present long-form writing has barely changed. This article is wrapped inside a header element, exactly the way some visual page builders emit their markup, which historically defeated naive readers.

Because the prose lives several nested divs below a header tag, a reader that strips every header outright will delete the entire article. The correct behaviour is to keep header and footer elements that actually contain substantial non-link text, and only remove the ones that are genuine chrome.

This third paragraph adds enough additional body text that the densest-container heuristic and the soft-chrome rule both agree the surrounding header is content, not navigation, so the article survives cleaning and renders in the reader column.

A fourth and final paragraph ensures the cleaned length comfortably clears the minimum threshold, so extraction reports success rather than falling back to restyle mode on this Framer-style page.
